newsitem.title: RUSSIA: U.S.'s Perry says he confident in Russia democracy.
newsitem.headline: U.S.'s Perry says he confident in Russia democracy.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry on Thursday expressed "great confidence" in Russia's democratic system despite a bitter public power struggle among members of President Boris Yeltsin's administration and staff.

"The Russian people have selected a democratic government. They have weathered many difficult problems since they selected that government and I have great confidence that they will continue to weather any problems that come up," Perry, on the second day of a visit to Russia, told reporters who asked if he was worried about security in Russia.
On Wednesday Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov accused Yeltsin's security chief Alexander Lebed of plotting a "creeping coup" while the president awaits heart surgery in mid-November.
Kulikov said he had ordered unspecified extra security measures across Russia but made clear they were not directly linked to his charges, which Lebed has hotly denied.
Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Thursday gave partial support to Kulikov, but he dismissed talk of "mutinies and putsches".

"I do not conceal my concern over the fact that a considerable part of what Minister Kulikov said corresponds with reality," Interfax news agency quoted Chernomyrdin as saying after meeting his top security staff to discuss the minister's allegations. But he added: "(I am) far from thinking about mutinies and putsches."
Perry said that Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov had not expressed any concerns to him about the political tensions in the Kremlin during their discussions on Wednesday.
"Minister Rodionov has expressed no such concerns to me and I have had long and detailed discussions with him," he added.

On Thursday Perry met first defence minister Andrei Kokoshin and was later due to address the Russian State Duma lower house of parliament to try and persuade deputies to ratify the Start-2 strategic arms reduction treaty.
